vip.etymology: From Middle English wyke , weke , from Old English wice , wucu ( “ week ” ) , from Proto-West Germanic * wikā , from Proto-Germanic * wikǭ ( “ sequence; week ” ) , from Proto-Indo-European * weyg- , * weyk- ( “ to bend, curve ” ) . Related to weak and dialectal English wick ( “ corner ” ) ; see Proto-Germanic * wīk(w)aną ( “ to bend, yield, cease ” ) .
